prompt_text: Who is the best roofing company in Dallas for a roof replacement?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single “best” roofing company for every situation — the right contractor depends on your needs (residential vs. commercial), roof type, budget, whether you’re filing an insurance claim, and your location in the Dallas–Fort Worth area. I can help you pick the best one for your job. To get you started, here’s a practical plan and vetting checklist.

Quick plan
- Get at least 3 written estimates from reputable local companies.
- Compare materials, labor, warranties, and cleanup/permit responsibilities — not just price.
- Verify insurance, certifications, references, and business longevity.
- Avoid storm-chaser contractors after storms; choose a local company with an established Dallas presence.

What to check when evaluating a roofer
- Insurance: Ask for proof of general liability insurance and workers’ compensation (or a signed waiver if they don’t carry it) and confirm the policy is current.
- Business verification: Confirm business address and phone, look up their Better Business Bureau (BBB) rating, and check Google/Yelp/Angi reviews and local references.
- Licenses/certs: In Texas some contractors carry manufacturer certifications (GAF Master Elite, CertainTeed SELECT ShingleMaster, etc.). These aren’t required by the state but are a good quality indicator.
- Warranty: Get both the manufacturer’s shingle warranty and the contractor’s workmanship warranty in writing. Understand the duration and any conditions.
- Written estimate/contract: Should include scope of work, materials (brand/style/color), tear-off vs. overlay, permit responsibility, timeline, payment schedule, and cleanup plans.
- Permits & inspections: Contractor should obtain all required city/county permits and schedule inspections if needed.
- Payment terms: Never pay full upfront. Typical is a deposit (often 10–30%), progress payments tied to milestones, and final payment after completion and lien releases.
- Cleanup & disposal: Confirm they will remove old roofing and dispose of debris, and request a final walk-through.
- Subcontractors: Ask whether the crew is employees or subcontractors and who will supervise the job.

Questions to ask every contractor
- How long have you operated in the Dallas area?
- Can you provide three local references with similar jobs?
- Are you a certified installer for the shingle manufacturer I want?
- Who will be the project supervisor, and will you obtain permits?
- What is your projected start and completion date?
- What is included in the warranty and what is excluded?

Red flags
- High-pressure tactics or demands for large immediate payments.
- No written estimate or vague contract.
- No insurance proof or refusal to provide references.
- Very low bid that seems too good to be true.
- Only a mobile phone number and no local office/address.

Where to look for reputable Dallas roofers
- Google Maps (check recent reviews and photos)
- Better Business Bureau (BBB)
- Angi / HomeAdvisor / Yelp
- Local Facebook/Nextdoor neighborhoods and your HOA
- Manufacturer locator tools (GAF, CertainTeed, Owens Corning) for certified contractors

If you want, I can:
- Suggest specific top-rated companies in your ZIP code (I’ll need your address or ZIP).
- Help draft a message or checklist to send to contractors.
- Compare 2–3 written estimates you receive and highlight differences.

Which would you like to do next? If you share your location (ZIP) and whether this is a residential or commercial job, I can give more targeted recommendations.
